title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 15
paragraphs: After this a message came to Mardonius that the Greeks were assembled at the Isthmus; so he marched back by way of Dekeleia. The chiefs of Boeotia had sent for those of the Asopians who dwelt near the line of march, and these were his guides along the road to Sphendaleis and from there to Tanagra. Having encamped for the night at Tanagra, and the next day having directed his march to Scolos, he was within Theban territory. Then he proceeded to cut down the trees in the lands of the Thebans, though they were on the Median side — moved not by enmity to them, but pressed by urgent necessity to make a defense for his camp, and also a refuge in case, when he engaged battle, things should not turn out as he desired. Now the encampment of his army stretched from Erythrai along Hysiai and reached the river Asopos; but he was not making the wall extend that far, rather about ten furlongs on each side.
